prerequisites: Physics and Mathematics in both years of High School
Physics and Mathematics in the first semester of the first year of this degree

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastery of basic concepts on the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application for solving engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Electric field and lines of force
Calculation of electric potential in continuous charge distributions
RC circuits. Charging and discharging a capacitor
Motion of a charge in a magnetic field
Torques on current loops and magnets
Fields created by moving charges and electric currents: Biot-Savart Law
Induced electromotive force and Faraday's Law
Alternating current in inductors and capacitors
Molecular and atomic spectra. Electromagnetic spectrum
teaching_methods: Professor-led problem-solving of exercises and problems for each topic, on-site
Individual problem-solving guided and reviewed by peers, on-site
assessment_rules: Two essential requirements to pass the course are active participation in all laboratory sessions and obtaining a minimum score of 4.0 in the final test. The final grade is calculated as 20% for the laboratory grade, 20% for the mid-term control, and 60% for the final test. The student must achieve a final grade of 5.0 or higher to pass the course. Students who do not pass in the ordinary call, or did not attend, may take the extraordinary call only for the re-evaluable assessment activities not passed. The laboratory grade is saved for 5 academic years.
